nonempty_sample.value: Purpose: altered-number Excel execution drills matched to the STRUCTURE of the 2026 A1S2 practice test. This is not an official Stellenbosch workbook and contains no assessment answers.
Build 200 resample means from the supplied with-replacement resamples; use the HTML for the training-only boundary rule and answer validator.
Use raw call-answer times for an upper-tail one-sample mean test with known population sigma; the HTML supplies the hypotheses, alpha, and power scenario.
Numerical answers in the HTML A1S2 mode are entered to exactly four decimals, with a full stop and no units.
The real 2026 practice test uses A1PTData.xlsx. This companion uses different data so that practice is not memorisation.

The real practice-test text does not reveal the exact lecturer convention for extracting 95% limits from 250 resamples. The HTML therefore labels its 200-resample cut-tail rule as a training convention, not an official 2026 procedure.
Do the calculation in Excel first. Return to the HTML only to enter/check the answer.
Correct answers and diagnostic feedback live in the HTML, not in this workbook.

Original sample is in green. Each row C:L is one with-replacement bootstrap resample of the same size. In M5 enter =AVERAGE(C5:L5) and fill down to M204. Do not treat the HTML's training cut-tail convention as an official 250-resample rule.

Use the HTML A1S2 Excel Mode for the hypotheses, alpha, known population standard deviation, critical-boundary and power questions. Compute from this worksheet in actual Excel before entering answers in the HTML.
You may place AVERAGE, COUNT, z-critical, critical X̄, test statistic, β and power calculations here.
